topic: Typed property graph schema definition with nodes and edges

title: PG-Schema: Schemas for Property Graphs
snippet: A typed graph schema defines a set of named labeled nodes with properties of specific data types, and a set of named labeled edges with structured properties of specific data types. A function associates each edge to a pair of object sets, where one set is called the tail and the other is called the head of an edge.
claim: Typed graph schemas define labeled nodes and edges with properties and type constraints for structural validation.

topic: Graph validity checking and type conformance
query: typed graph database schema definition nodes edges validation
title: Schema-Based Query Optimisation for Graph Databases
snippet: For validating a graph against a graph type, nodes are identified that conform to each node type, and this information is used to identify edges that conform to each edge type through an analogous procedure. In distributed graph databases, a schema is used to validate write queries before they are transmitted to database shards.
claim: Schema validation identifies conforming nodes and edges; distributed systems validate writes before transmission.

topic: In-memory graph interface with O(1) complexity operations
query: in-memory graph structure validity checking interface implementation edges
title: Chapter 4. Basic data types and interface
snippet: The GraphInterface includes methods `numVertices` and `numEdges` which return a count of vertices or edges of a graph, and a method `numNeighbors` that returns a count of outbound neighbors for a given vertex. These methods have O(1) complexity. The `iterateNeighbors` method takes a dense identifier and a callback/lambda, which is called for every neighbor of the given vertex.
claim: In-memory graph interfaces provide O(1) vertex/edge counting and callback-based neighbor iteration.

title: JGraphT -- A Java library for graph data structures and algorithms
snippet: The Graph interface, at the top of the hierarchy, defines all high-level graph operations. The class AbstractGraph offers a minimal implementation of this Graph interface, without explicitly defining the data structures for storage and indexing as these are managed by the graph backend.
claim: Graph interfaces separate operations from storage backend, allowing flexibility in implementation choice.

title: CSCI 581 (Object-Oriented Design) Lecture Notes on Data Abstraction
snippet: Separation of interface from implementation is used to divide the class into two parts, commonly referred to as the private part and the public part. The implementer has the flexibility to change the module as long as the module still satisfies its interface. The interface ensures that the module is loosely coupled to its clients.
claim: Interface abstraction provides implementer flexibility while maintaining loose coupling with clients.
